newsitem.title: UK: Sedgwick up, paper highlights stakebuilding.
newsitem.headline: Sedgwick up, paper highlights stakebuilding.

text.p: Shares in Sedgwick Plc rose on Wednesday, adding to Tuesday's gain as a report in the Financial Times highlighted a purchase of stock by U.S. fund manager Oakmark International.
Shares in the insurance broker were up 3p at 127-1/2 by 0802 GMT, adding to a 3p rise on Tuesday as the stock bounced from a year's low of 113p set last week.
Sedgwick said on Tuesday Oakmark had bought 800,000 shares, taking its stake to 3.11 percent.

The FT pointed out that Oakmark was managed by David Herro, best known in the UK for leading a shareholder revolt that led to the ousting of Maurice Saatchi from the advertising group that bore his name.
It said there was speculation that Herro's presence on Sedgwick's share register could signal pressure for corporate changes.
A spokeswoman for Sedgwick said it had held several meetings with Herro as part of its normal programme of contacts with institutional investors, but declined further comment.
She said questions about the reasons for Oakmark's purchase of stock should be addressed to Herro himself.
